sections.html:
Belton is the seat of Bell County in Central Texas, and it keeps getting bigger. It had 18,216 residents in 2010 and 23,054 in 2020. The July 1, 2025 estimate is 25,964, a 12.7% rise over the 2020 estimates base. The median value of an owner-occupied home is $258,700, and 56.0% of homes are lived in by their owners. Renters pay a median of $1,252 a month, so rentals are a real slice of local housing.

Steady demand helps, but a seller still has a tax bill to square away, maybe a tenant to deal with, and a deed to sign. The sections below cover Belton details first and the Texas rules after them. If you own an older lot near Nolan Creek, ask about floodplain status early, because buyers and their lenders will.

sections.h2: Property tax bills and early-payment discounts
sections.html:
Bell CAD appraises property and also takes the payments. Each October it sends one statement for the entire year. The money is due on receipt, and anything still open after January 31 picks up penalties on February 1. A full early payment earns a discount from certain taxing entities, as shown below.

Bell CAD payment timing for a full-year bill
Payment monthDiscount for paying in full
October3%
November2%
December1%
JanuaryBase tax, no discount and no penalty
February 1 onwardPenalties begin
  • Payment options include online, phone, or a visit to a district office.
  • The Belton office has a drop box outside for after-hours payments.
  • Deferral, quarterly installment and homestead delinquent installment agreements are explained on the district's site.

Bell CAD does, with offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple. It reviews sales and properties every year, so a value can change from one notice to the next. Put your most recent notice in your closing folder, because buyers like to see what the house is carried at.

The filing window runs January 1 to April 30, and you can file at the district office or online. Once approved, the exemption rolls forward on its own. Renewal comes up only if the chief appraiser sends a request or you change homes. Bell CAD will also accept a late filing for two years after the tax goes delinquent.

To qualify, the property has to be your home as of January 1, and no other house can carry a homestead claim for you. State law caps the land at 20 acres, but the district describes an acre or less as the usual case. Someone who owns a mobile home on rented land can still apply with a title or a verified purchase contract.

Older and disabled owners get extra relief. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older can keep the school tax ceiling. A disabled veteran brings a VA letter showing at least a 10% rating, and a 100% rating may support a full homestead exemption.

sections.h2: Does the 10% homestead cap change what a buyer pays?
sections.html:
The cap touches assessed value only. Market value moves with sales and has no ceiling, but a homestead's assessed value is held to 10% growth a year. That protection begins after the owner has held the home through one full January 1.

So a buyer who purchases a house at a price far above its old assessment may see the tax bill step up for a few years, until the assessment reaches market value. If your buyer plans to live in the house, tell them to expect that.

Belton adopted its short-term rental ordinance on March 13, 2023. Every rental needs a city permit good for one year, and the renewal filing is due within 30 days of expiration. The city won't renew until local hotel and motel occupancy tax has been paid.

A rental the owner doesn't occupy must stay at least 500 feet from another short-term rental. Each address needs its own application through the online portal, and income is reported there quarterly, with zero entered for months without stays.

  • Apply and renew through the city's portal.
  • File one application per property address.
  • Call the Planning Department with questions about the process.

If you rented the house this way, settle the tax filings before closing so nothing trails you after the sale.

sections.h2: Tenants in the house before closing
sections.html:
An eviction in Texas opens with a written notice to vacate. Three days is the minimum unless the lease says otherwise. Delivery can be by hand, by leaving it inside the unit, by mail, or by email if the lease permits that.

When the tenant doesn't leave, the landlord files in justice court and a hearing is set 10 to 21 days out. Either side has five days after judgment to appeal to county court. Six days after judgment a writ of possession can be issued, and the tenant gets 24 hours of warning before removal. Add those steps to your timeline when you pick a closing date, or arrange a sale in which the tenant stays.

Most Texas loans let the lender auction the house at the courthouse, and Bell County sales happen on the first Tuesday of a month. After the default letter arrives you have 20 days to bring the loan current. The lender then has to give notice of sale at least 21 days before the auction. If you can't catch up, a sale before that Tuesday is often how owners keep some equity.

Property tax is a separate matter. Its lien attaches on January 1 and stays with the land through any sale. The person who owned the house that day remains liable, so the title company should clear the year's bill at the closing table.

sections.h2: Where a Belton deed is filed
sections.html:
Deeds for Bell County land are recorded with the county clerk. The deed must be signed and acknowledged. After it is on file, ask Bell CAD what paperwork it wants before it changes the owner name on the account.

The state clerk manual puts the recording fee at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every page after it, plus other statutory charges. Call the clerk for the exact total. In most sales the title company handles recording and mails you a copy afterward.

A listing brings showings, a buyer's mortgage, an appraisal and a round of repair requests once the inspection is done. A cash sale skips most of those steps, which leaves clear title as the main thing that sets the timeline. Whatever offer you consider, get it in writing first. Then ask the title company to confirm the tax payoff, any liens and every person who has to sign the deed.

A simple order of work helps. Pull your latest tax statement and appraisal notice, get a mortgage payoff figure if there is a loan, gather any lease and rental permit paperwork, and note any floodplain or repair history on the lot. With those in a folder, a buyer can price the house quickly and the closing goes faster.

faqs.q: When must a Belton homestead application be filed?
faqs.a: By April 30 for the tax year. Bell CAD still takes late applications for up to two years after the tax turns delinquent, and no yearly renewal is required.

faqs.q: Is there an early-pay discount on Belton property tax?
faqs.a: Yes, for certain entities. It is 3% in October, 2% in November and 1% in December, with the base amount due in January.

faqs.q: Can I rent a Belton house on a nightly basis?
faqs.a: Only with a city permit. Belton requires one for every short-term rental, renewed yearly, and a rental the owner doesn't live in must sit 500 feet from any other.

faqs.q: If I sell a Belton house mid-year, who owes that year's tax?
faqs.a: The owner on January 1 carries the lien and the liability. Sellers and buyers usually divide the bill at closing through the title company.

faqs.q: Which office values my Belton house?
faqs.a: Bell CAD does, with offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple. It normally reviews sales and properties every year.
